verdicts.reason: Both are the same competent three-column banner. A wraps the headline as 'Move ten minutes / today', leaving 'today' as a near-orphan, and its CTA sits only about 20px from the right edge. B's 'Move ten / minutes today' break is better balanced and its subcopy has more breathing room, but its CTA is just as tight to the right edge and there is a slightly larger gap between the phone and the text.

A keeps the CTA large and vertically centred against the headline, though it crowds the right edge and 'today' is left almost alone on its line. B shrinks the 'Try It Free' button to a tiny pill dropped in the bottom-right corner, so the main action is buried and lines up with nothing. The headline also floats with a large gap above the subcopy.

A shrinks the phone, the key product image, to an unreadable thumbnail-sized icon stranded under the CTA. That loses the design's main visual and leaves the left half and the top empty. B keeps the phone at full size with the headline and CTA in a clear left-to-right flow, apart from a cramped right margin on the CTA and the near-orphan 'today'.
